author: WP03
summary: A worked first game (skeleton, movement, clamped bounce with sound, rectangle collision, renderer independence). The API calls are current at TARGET, but several explanations were imprecise (the 'content model' framing, frame-rate independence under fixed step, viewport semantics) and the bounce example replayed its sound every update. libcna.com already had the skeleton and lifecycle basics in getting-started, the game-loop guide and tutorials 03-16; the line-by-line reasoning, the CNAEXT-versus-XNA portability notes and the strict Intersects edge case were missing and now live on a new walkthrough deep dive with syntax-checked programs.

concepts.text: The first program is a complete translation unit built from the XNA-style skeleton; the CMake target and the named asset files are project inputs, and the deeper framework contracts are explained separately.

target.evidence: framing of the walkthrough; no TARGET fact

concepts.text: The minimal CNA game derives from Game, owns a GraphicsDeviceManager constructed against itself, creates its SpriteBatch and Texture2D in LoadContent, overrides Update/Draw with base calls, and main() constructs the game and calls Run().

target.evidence: modules/runtime/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Game.hpp (Game); syntax-checked with g++ -fsyntax-only against TARGET headers

concepts.note: Recreated with base calls and without Present(); the site's getting-started skeleton still calls Present() inside Draw and omits the base calls (reported).

concepts.text: Every include follows the XNA namespace path (Microsoft/Xna/Framework/...), so no CNA-specific include is needed to boot a game; the only systematic spelling change is the getXProperty() accessor convention.

Unlike FNA, the Game base constructor already builds its own GraphicsDevice before a derived constructor creates the GraphicsDeviceManager; the manager registers services and, in DoInitialize, applies its preferences by resetting that same device instead of creating a second one.

LoadContent() is the correct point for GPU resources: a derived constructor can already reach the live default device, but that is before the manager's preference reset, so the reason to defer is the reset, not a missing renderer.
concepts.note: Tutorial 04 still says the device does not exist in the constructor (Phase-1 error reported).

concepts.text: The file path "assets/logo.png" loads because Texture2D has a CNAEXT file-path constructor that decodes a loose image; the XNA-style ContentManager route resolves .xnb, then .cnb, then a loose file (the older 'raw asset plus JSON descriptor content model' framing is not how TARGET describes content).
Update takes a mutable GameTime& while Draw takes a const GameTime&, matching the XNA signatures; rendering must not change timing state.

Game::Update(gameTime) runs the registered updateable components and then FrameworkDispatcher::Update(); omitting it silently stops dynamic audio, media and touch polling. Game::Draw(gameTime) draws the drawable components.
Draw clears with Color::CornflowerBlue, the clear colour of XNA's generated project templates, and uses the SpriteBatch Begin()/Draw()/End() triad.

Application Draw() never calls GraphicsDevice::Present(): after the override returns Game::EndDraw() delegates to the manager, which presents exactly once whatever renderer is active; a Present() inside Draw presents every frame twice.

main() needs only two game-specific lines, construct and Run(), because window creation, renderer initialization, the timing loop and shutdown live in Game; the shape mirrors XNA's Program.Main so porting an entry point is close to mechanical.

concepts.section: A second program: making it move
concepts.text: SpriteBatch::Draw(texture, float x, float y) is a CNAEXT convenience overload, not XNA 4.0; portable code should use Draw(texture, Vector2 position, Color color).

target.evidence: modules/graphics/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Graphics/SpriteBatch.hpp (CNAEXT Draw(const Texture2D&, float, float); Draw(const Texture2D&, Vector2, Color))

concepts.section: A second program: making it move
concepts.text: Keyboard::GetState() is a static call returning a fresh immutable KeyboardState snapshot; there is no keyboard object to own, and the snapshot is published once per tick before the updates.

concepts.section: A second program: making it move
concepts.text: Speed times ElapsedGameTime.TotalSeconds gives frame-rate independence; the claim that a flat per-Update step moves faster on a higher-refresh display holds only for variable step, because under the default fixed step updates run at the target rate whatever the display does.

concepts.section: A third program: bouncing off the edges, with sound
concepts.text: The bounds check must clamp in the same branch that detects the crossing; otherwise holding a key accumulates position off-screen and the sprite must travel back through the overshoot.

target.evidence: game-logic reasoning; no CNA API fact

concepts.section: A third program: bouncing off the edges, with sound
concepts.text: Bounds come from GraphicsDevice's Viewport, the logical draw space; with the default Letterbox mode the viewport stays the back-buffer size when the window is resized (the older reasoning that it tracks the resized back buffer is imprecise).

concepts.section: A third program: bouncing off the edges, with sound
concepts.text: SoundEffect's file-path constructor is a CNAEXT convenience (XNA loads SoundEffect through the content pipeline); Play() uses default volume, pitch and pan, and Play(volume, pitch, pan) varies them.

target.evidence: modules/audio/include/Microsoft/Xna/Framework/Audio/SoundEffect.hpp (CNAEXT SoundEffect(const std::string&); Play(); Play(float, float, float))

concepts.section: A third program: bouncing off the edges, with sound
concepts.text: In the bounce example the edge flag stays true on every update while the key is held (including catch-up updates), so the sound must be triggered on the transition into the edge rather than every frame.

target.evidence: example logic re-derived; syntax-checked translation unit

concepts.note: The original example played the sound on every update at the edge.

concepts.text: Collision rectangles are rebuilt every update from the same position fields Draw reads and the texture sizes; Rectangle takes int x/y/width/height, so float positions need static_cast<int>.

Rectangle::Intersects is strict: two 100x100 rectangles at (0,0) and (100,0) share an edge and do not intersect; only non-zero overlap counts, pinned by RectangleTests.IntersectsAdjacentRectanglesReturnsFalse.

concepts.section: What happens if you change the renderer
concepts.text: Nothing in the game source names a renderer: reconfiguring the same file with -DCNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER=VULKAN instead of OPENGLES3 changes the backend underneath while the game-facing code stays unchanged.
concepts.note: Not run on each renderer; stated as contract.
